description:
pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:1469:

    pub fn check_shape(
        cert: &Certificate,
        kind: SubjectKind,
        now_unix: u64,
        profile: &dyn LintProfile,
    ) -> Result<(), Vec<Finding>>

The shape is:
  - Ok(())  — no Error/Fatal findings
  - Err(findings) — has at least one Error/Fatal; returns ALL findings

The documented contract (line 1447-1450) acknowledges this:
'Findings on Warn-only certs are silently discarded by check_shape
(the Ok variant carries no findings). Callers that need access to
Warn-level findings even on pass should call LintRunner::run_cert
directly via profile.lint_runner().'

This is exactly the defensive-code-forcing shape AGENTS.md warns
against. Three problems:

1. *Inconsistent information density across branches.* Err carries
   the full Vec<Finding>; Ok throws it away. The caller who wants
   to log every Warn finding for compliance reporting has to call
   the function and *also* call run_cert separately, evaluating the
   same lints twice. That's an API gotcha, not a convenience.

2. *Caller cannot tell why ok happened.* Was it because no lint
   fired, because every lint was NotApplicable, because the lint set
   was empty? Same Ok(()) for all three cases. Downstream report
   generators want to distinguish 'we ran 47 lints, 47 passed' from
   'we ran 47 lints, 47 returned NotApplicable because the cert
   wasn't a TLS leaf'.

3. *Implicit re-evaluation cost.* The recommended workaround (call
   `profile.lint_runner().run_cert(...)` to get warnings even on
   pass) re-runs the entire lint set. For a check_shape on a high-
   volume cert intake, that doubles the cost.

# The right contract shape

Either:

  (a) Return Vec<Finding> directly. Callers filter by
      f.result.is_finding() and decide what they want. This is
      idiomatic and matches LintRunner::run_cert (which returns
      Vec<Finding>). 'check_shape' becomes a thin wrapper that
      just calls run_cert and returns its result.

  (b) Return Result<Vec<Finding>, Vec<Finding>> — the Vec carries
      *all* findings in both branches; the Ok/Err distinction is
      purely the actionability question 'did anything fail?'

  (c) Return a typed verdict struct:
        ShapeResult {
            verdict: enum { Pass, Failed },
            findings: Vec<Finding>,
        }
      with #[non_exhaustive] for forward-compat. This is the most
      explicit and matches OSCAL Assessment Results modeling.

The current shape forces every defensive-minded caller (e.g. one
that ships an audit log) to write the boilerplate:

    let findings = profile.lint_runner().run_cert(cert, kind, 0, now_unix);
    let any_error = findings.iter().any(|f| matches!(
        f.result, LintResult::Error(_) | LintResult::Fatal(_)));
    if any_error { ... }

That's exactly what check_shape() does internally. There's no point
in the helper if every caller has to recreate it for warnings.

# Forward fit

This API was added in commit 5c0d67de (this diff). Removing the
discard is non-breaking pre-1.0. Cheap fix: change the signature to
Result<Vec<Finding>, Vec<Finding>> and adjust the body to return
findings in both branches.
title: API contract: check_shape() silently discards Warn findings on Ok path
